title: fix: stop Grafana reloading with stale session cookies
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes Grafana repeatedly reloading after Pollinations sign-in when an old `grafana_session_expiry` cookie remains. Grafana otherwise attempts its own token renewal, receives 401, and reloads.
- Clears only that obsolete metadata on authenticated Grafana responses, for both `/` and `/grafana/`. Pollinations sessions and the trusted identity proxy stay intact.
- Adds four direct gateway regression tests and runs them before the existing deployment checks.
- Verified locally against the real Grafana 11.4.0 image: before the fix, 19 dashboard loads and 18 renewal attempts; afterward, one load and zero renewals with the same stale-cookie fixture. Overview and charts render with existing read-only Tinybird credentials; local alerting disabled. Clean-session and refresh checks also pass.
- Validation: regression tests, Biome, frontend/Worker build, Docker image, and deployment dry run pass. Nothing merged or deployed.

gist.headline: Grafana Stops Chasing Its Tail
gist.blurb: A stale Grafana cookie was making dashboards repeatedly knock on the auth door. The gateway now quietly clears that one obsolete breadcrumb, and the charts get on with their day.
gist.summary: Authenticated Grafana responses for both `/` and `/grafana/` now clear the obsolete `grafana_session_expiry` cookie, preventing Grafana 11.4.0 from triggering its own failed token-renewal loop after Pollinations sign-in.
gist.impact: Dashboards with an old Grafana expiry cookie now load once with zero renewal attempts instead of repeatedly reloading, while Pollinations sessions and the trusted identity proxy remain intact.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a tiny observability mechanic in a tool belt gently removing one dusty, expired cookie label from a cozy CRT dashboard terminal. The monitor robot happily watches stable charts bloom like code-plants, with a small looped-arrow vine visibly untangled; this represents preserving the existing trusted session while stopping the redundant Grafana refresh cycle.
